assessment: Evidence supports a recurring, escalating upstream microbiological excursion pattern on three RELEASED batches of Famotidine Injection, USP (BATCH-075, BATCH-084, BATCH-099) between 2024-12 and 2025-03: upstream bioburden action-limit exceedances of 1.23, 1.48 and 1.71 vs an action limit of 1.0, each with an open, high-severity microbiology deviation (DEV-0003/0005/0009) and no recorded root cause or CAPA. All three batches passed release endotoxin/sterility testing and were released. On 2025-10-20 a pyrogenic-type symptom complaint (CMP-0001) was filed against released BATCH-075, followed on 2025-10-27 by an out-of-specification endotoxin result (LAB-0303, 1.37 vs specification limit 1.0, review status out_of_specification). No deviation, CAPA, investigation or other follow-up record exists after 2025-10-27 as of the 2026-10-15 cutoff. Root cause is NOT established. Two independent child investigations found the manufacturing-side records (historian, operator events, maintenance) routine with no out-of-range process events, pointing to the laboratory/EM signal domain; child findings on equipment links (WO-0008/VESSEL-01) and EM organism (gram-negative morphology on EM-0100) could not be verified by the lead before the tool budget was exhausted. The evidence package is labeled synthetic/simulated factory records (source review: 'SYNTHETIC FACTORY RECORDS'; complaints flagged public_or_synthetic=synthetic), so regulatory weight should be confirmed by human reviewers. No product disposition, release, recall or CAPA action is taken or approved by this report.

unknowns: Shared equipment use across the three batches is child-reported and unverified.
No organism identification beyond the unverified 'gram-negative morphology' report.
No water-system or cleaning records in the retrieved evidence.

resolved_questions.question: Were there action-level upstream microbiological excursions on released batches?
resolved_questions.finding: Yes: verified 1.23 (BATCH-075) plus tool-returned 1.48 (BATCH-084) and 1.71 (BATCH-099) vs action limit 1.0, with open deviations on all three.

resolved_questions.question: Was there a post-release quality signal on BATCH-075?
resolved_questions.finding: Yes: pyrogenic-type complaint CMP-0001 (2025-10-20) followed by out-of-specification endotoxin result LAB-0303 at 137% of limit (2025-10-27).

resolved_questions.question: Were the excursion batches released before or after passing release testing?
resolved_questions.finding: After: dispositions (2024-12-16, 2025-01-19, 2025-03-27) post-date passing endotoxin specification ratios and 'no growth' sterility results for each batch.

resolved_questions.question: What is the product and scope of concern?
resolved_questions.finding: Famotidine Injection, USP; three released batches (BATCH-075, BATCH-084, BATCH-099) with upstream micro excursions, plus a complaint and endotoxin OOS on BATCH-075.

open_questions: What is the origin of LAB-0303 (retention retest, new sample, or data error), and why does its availability_type read 'requires_new_test'?
Why was no deviation, CAPA or investigation record opened for complaint CMP-0001 or the LAB-0303 out-of-specification result between 2025-10-27 and the 2026-10-15 cutoff?
Is distributed BATCH-075 (and related lots BATCH-084, BATCH-099) still in market, and was any recall/field-action assessment performed? No evidence either way.
Is the 'gram-negative morphology' organism on EM-0100 real (child-reported, unverified), and is there any species-level identification anywhere in the quality system?

Do BATCH-xxx and SYN-xxx identifiers refer to the same physical batches (entity aliasing), e.g., lims_review_local lot 'SYN-0075' and historian batch 'SYN-0075' vs LIMS 'BATCH-075'? reconcile_entities could not be run.
Were other batches besides 075/084/099 affected by the same upstream pattern (search breadth was limited by tool budget)?
What are the local review/QA statuses for the release results of the three batches (only LAB-0303's review status was retrieved)?

Are the child-reported routine manufacturing findings (no out-of-range historian events; WO-0008 planned inspection on VESSEL-01 the evening before the BATCH-084 deviation; routine operator events) accurate? The lead could not verify them.
